title: Enhanced Subgraph Learning in 2-FWL GNNs via Local Connectivity, Spectral, and Distance Encodings

problem.claim: 2-FWL GNNs have a gap between theoretical expressiveness and practical performance.

gap.claim: Existing graph structural encodings lack sufficient sensitivity to subtle local connectivity, spectral, and distance-based variations.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes CSDGSE, a graph structural encoding framework combining exact local connectivity, full-frequency spectral features, and full-range distance interactions.
The paper introduces a scalable divide-and-conquer algorithm for computing exact local connectivity across all node pairs.
The authors report that CSDGSE outperforms existing graph structural encodings on complex structural patterns and molecular property prediction benchmarks including ZINC.

stated_novelty.claim: CSDGSE is presented as a novel graph structural encoding framework, with its scalable exact-local-connectivity computation described as a key innovation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that CSDGSE outperforms existing graph structural encodings.
The authors report state-of-the-art results on molecular property prediction benchmarks such as ZINC.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work addresses the gap between the theoretical capacity and practical performance of 2-FWL GNNs.
It attributes the gap to insufficient sensitivity in existing structural encodings, including incomplete spectral and distance sensitivity and weak local-connectivity capture.
It proposes CSDGSE to jointly improve local connectivity, spectral, and distance sensitivity, supported by a scalable exact-connectivity algorithm.
The authors report improved performance and state-of-the-art results on structural-pattern and molecular-property benchmarks.
The work frames enhanced structural sensitivity as a way to align theoretical expressiveness with practical effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Existing encodings may miss practically important structural information despite being used with theoretically expressive models.

interpretation.claim: Model expressiveness alone may not yield practical gains when the representation does not preserve the relevant structural distinctions.

application.claim: When improving expressive graph models, evaluate and strengthen representation sensitivity across local, spectral, and long-range structural dimensions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported graph tasks or benchmarks.

unknowns: Exact model architecture and integration details are unspecified.
Benchmark set, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
Computational cost and scalability measurements are not reported.
Experimental protocol and independent verification are not described.
